name: Śrī Advaita Ācārya Prabhu
add: Nandgram Dham: born in 1434 at Navagrāma, Śrīhaṭṭa district (eastern Bengal); the bhakta-avatāra, incarnation of Mahā-Viṣṇu, one with Sadāśiva (Gaura-gaṇoddeśa-dīpikā 11, 76; Caitanya-caritāmṛta Ādi 1.12); his seat, Śāntipura on the Gaṅgā in Nadia.

name: Śrī Akṣobhya Tīrtha
add: Nandgram Dham: born Govinda Śāstrī (also Govinda Bhaṭṭa). Who ordained him is disputed: the Vyāsarāja Maṭha's own record names Mādhava Tīrtha, his predecessor; B. N. K. Sharma names Padmanābha Tīrtha; some devotional accounts, Madhvācārya himself. Pontiff traditionally 1350–1365, the fourth after Madhva; chief disciple and successor Jayatīrtha. At Mulbagal he defeated the Advaitin Vidyāraṇya in debate on «tat tvam asi»; a stone pillar there remembers it. He founded the Kūḍli Akṣobhya Tīrtha Maṭha near Shivamogga, continued by his disciple Trailokya-bhūṣaṇa Tīrtha.

name: Anupama
add: Nandgram Dham: born Śrī Vallabha, youngest son of Kumāradeva, younger brother of Sanātana and Rūpa; Śrī Caitanya named him «Anupama Mallika» at Rāmakeli. He reportedly headed Husain Shah's mint (Bhakti-ratnākara). From childhood he worshipped Lord Rāmacandra (Raghunātha). Father of Śrīla Jīva Gosvāmī.

name: Śrī Baladeva Vidyābhūṣaṇa
add: Nandgram Dham: born in a vaiśya farming family near Remuṇā; dīkṣā from Rādhā-dāmodara at Jagannātha Purī, śikṣā from Viśvanātha Cakravartī in Vṛndāvana; also called Govinda dāsa. His Govinda-bhāṣya is the first commentary of the Gauḍīya sampradāya on the Vedānta-sūtra. Traditionally left this world in 1768 in Vṛndāvana; some scholars place it as late as 1793 (disputed).

name: Vāsudeva Kusthi
add: Nandgram Dham: the Lord met him on the road outside Kūrma Vipra's house at Kūrmakṣetra (Śrīkūrmam) during His tour of South India, his body covered with open, worm-infested sores; after curing him the Lord received the name «Vāsudevāmṛta-prada», giver of nectar to Vāsudeva (Caitanya-caritāmṛta Madhya 7.136–150).

name: Bhagavān Ācārya
add: Nandgram Dham: titled Nyāyācārya, «master of logic»; born in Navadvīpa and raised at Hālisahara (24 Parganas). Father Śatānanda Khān; sons Raghunātha Ācārya and Rāmanātha; younger brother Gopāla Bhaṭṭācārya. An incarnation of a cowherd boy (Caitanya-caritāmṛta Antya 2.85). He cooked for the Lord and hosted Him (Ādi 10; Antya 2, 5, 8, 14).

name: Bhagavān Paṇḍit
add: Nandgram Dham: named only once, in Caitanya-caritāmṛta Ādi 10.69, as the thirtieth branch of the Lord's tree, between Kholāvecā Śrīdhara (29th) and Jagadīśa Paṇḍita (31st): «an extremely dear servant of the Lord», in whom Kṛṣṇa was already established before this life. His birth, death, family, guru and pastimes are not recorded anywhere.

name: Śrīla Bhakti Siddhānta Sarasvatī
add: Nandgram Dham: born at 3:30 pm on 6 February 1874 in Purī, the sixth child of Bhāgavatī Devī and the seventh of Bhaktivinoda Ṭhākura's fourteen children; as a small boy he learned the Bhagavad-gītā by heart in Sanskrit.

name: Śrīla Bhaktivinoda Ṭhākura
add: Nandgram Dham: born Kedāranātha Datta, of a Datta kāyastha family whose line goes back to Kṛṣṇānanda Datta, an associate of Nityānanda Prabhu. First married in 1850, at twelve, to five-year-old Śyāmāṇī Mitra of Rāṇāghāṭa. Studied at the village school of Ulā, then at the Hindu Charitable Institution and Hindu College, Calcutta.

name: Bhūgarbha Gosvāmī
add: Nandgram Dham: Lokanātha Gosvāmī was his relative (his paternal uncle, by one account) or simply his lifelong friend; sources differ. Named in Caitanya-caritāmṛta Ādi 12.82 and Madhya 18.50. His birth is not recorded; he left this world on the Caturdaśī of the bright fortnight of Kārtika (year unknown).

name: Bijalī Khān
add: Nandgram Dham: «Vijulī Khān» in the Caitanya-caritāmṛta; a Pathān, son of a local Muslim ruler (rājāra kumāra). His companion Rāmadāsa was an elder Sufi among the same troop of horsemen, initiated moments before him (Madhya 18.163–212).

name: Bilvamaṅgala Ṭhākura
add: Nandgram Dham: also written Vilvamaṅgala; his time is disputed, from the 9th to the 14th century; born in South India (the Kerala tradition and Śrīla Prabhupāda's purport point to different regions).

name: Śrī Brahmaṇya Tīrtha
add: Nandgram Dham: before sannyāsa, Narasiṁhācārya. He headed the maṭha at Abbūr, Karnataka, a line later called the Vyāsarāja Maṭha; his most famous disciple was Vyāsa Tīrtha, later rājaguru of the Vijayanagara empire. Mid-15th century; he left this world in 1467 or 1475–1476 (sources disagree).

name: Vuddhimanta Khan
add: Nandgram Dham: the thirty-sixth branch of the Lord's tree (Caitanya-caritāmṛta Ādi 10.74); with his friend Mukunda Sañjaya, among the richest men of Navadvīpa. Bhaktivinoda Ṭhākura identifies him as King Suvarṇa Sena of Satya-yuga, born again (also in Caitanya-bhāgavata and Bhakti-ratnākara).
